prompt.context: Our client is the designer and publisher of Day Fort, a free-to-play multiplayer shooting game. Over the past 5 years, Day Fort has broken both revenue and profit records for the gaming industry. However, the client's profitability has declined recently. Your client has hired you to help them improve the profitability of Day Fort.
prompt.question: How can the client improve the profitability of Day Fort?

clarifying_info.q: How does Day Fort make money if it is free to play?
clarifying_info.a: Through selling customizable skins (outfits) for the in-game characters and selling season 'battle passes' that allow players to unlock skins by playing the game.

clarifying_info.q: How do they source their skins?
clarifying_info.a: They are made, for free, by the community of players.
People purchase the game on their computer and are from all over the world.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific profitability target?

exhibits.title: Online multiplayer games profit pool (2014-2018)
exhibits.shows: A bar or line chart showing annual profit ($M) from 2014 to 2018 for several online multiplayer games: Day Fort, CS: Stop, Day G, PUB A, and Other. The y-axis runs from 0 to 30 ($M).

data.note: Individual values readable from chart; y-axis scale 0-30 ($M)

exhibits.title: Online multiplayer games market research survey results
exhibits.shows: A chart comparing Day Fort, Day G, and CS: Stop across four dimensions rated on an Importance/Performance scale of 1-10: New Features, Item Trading Allowed, Game Play, and Community.

framework: Understand revenue streams (skins, battle passes) and cost structure
Benchmark competitor profitability trends to identify if issue is company-specific or industry-wide
Analyze customer preferences vs. competitor offerings to find capability gaps
Quantify profit impact of closing key gaps
Formulate recommendation with implementation steps and risks

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell us about Day Fort's profitability relative to competitors and the industry?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that Day Fort is the ONLY game whose profitability declined between 2017 and 2018. The industry as a whole grew. An exceptional candidate will note Day Fort's profitability fell ~10% from 2017 to 2018 while the industry overall rose ~10%, representing a ~20-percentage-point relative swing.

math.setup: Read approximate Day Fort profit values from chart for 2017 and 2018; compute percent change. Industry total change can also be computed.
steps: Day Fort 2017 ≈ higher value; Day Fort 2018 ≈ lower value => ~10% decline
math.answer: Day Fort is the only game losing profitability; industry is growing ~10% while Day Fort shrinks ~10%.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 2 tell us about where Day Fort is underperforming relative to competitors?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note Day Fort scores at or near the top in New Features (9), Game Play (9), and Community (9), but scores only 5 on Item Trading Allowed while CS: Stop scores 10 and Day G scores 9. Item Trading Allowed therefore represents the key gap. Candidate should recommend allowing item trading.

questions.prompt: If the client allows item trading, how does profitability change? Use the following data: 125M players. Current: 1% buy items, $10 avg spend/year, 100% margin. If trading allowed: 10% buy items, $3 avg spend/year, 50% margin.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate current profit and projected profit, then size the uplift. No mistakes in arithmetic expected.

math.setup: Profit = Players × % purchasing × avg spend × margin
math.answer: Current profit = $12.5M; new profit = $18.75M; increase = $6.25M (~50% improvement)

recommendation: The client should begin allowing in-game item trading. Day Fort trails competitors significantly on this dimension (score 5 vs. 9-10 for rivals) and it is highly important to players.
Implementing item trading is projected to increase annual profit by $6.25M, approximately a 50% uplift from the current $12.5M.
risks: The community may not respond well to the change in the skins economy—if players devalue skins, spending could drop further.
Effective trading systems used by competitors may be patented, forcing the client to build a novel system without prior expertise.
next_steps: Work with the development team to design and build out an in-game trading system.
Analyze competitor trading systems (CS: Stop, Day G) to identify best practices and patent landscape before building.
